Introduction

What Is a Trademark?

A trademark is a distinctive sign — a name, logo, tagline or combination — that identifies your goods or services and distinguishes them from competitors. Registration under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 gives you exclusive nationwide rights to use that mark for the classes of goods or services you register it under.

Registering early protects your brand as it grows, and gives you clear legal standing to act against anyone using a confusingly similar mark.

Why Register

What Trademark Registration Protects

🛡️

Exclusive Nationwide Rights

Exclusive right to use your mark across India for the classes of goods or services registered.

⚖️

Legal Standing

Clear legal grounds to act against infringement, unlike an unregistered mark which relies on harder-to-prove passing-off claims.

💼

Brand Asset Value

A registered trademark becomes a transferable, licensable business asset with real commercial value.

™️

Right to Use the ® Symbol

Only registered trademarks can legally display the ® symbol, signalling protected status to competitors.

Eligibility

What Can Be Registered

  • Any individual, Proprietorship, Partnership, LLP, Company or Trust can apply
  • Brand names, logos, taglines, or a combination of these
  • The mark must be distinctive and not merely descriptive of the goods/services
  • The mark should not conflict with an existing registered trademark in the same class

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Trademark Search

We conduct a search to check for identical or confusingly similar existing marks before filing.

2. Application Filing

The application is filed with the Trade Marks Registry under the correct class(es) of goods or services.

3. Examination

The Registry examines the application and may raise objections, which we respond to on your behalf.

4. Publication & Opposition Period

If accepted, the mark is published in the Trade Marks Journal for a period during which third parties can oppose it.

5. Registration

If unopposed or the opposition is resolved in your favour, the trademark is registered. The overall process commonly takes 18–24 months; timelines can vary significantly.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN and address proof of the applicant/entity
  • A clear representation of the logo or mark, if applicable
  • Proof of first use of the mark, if already in use
  • Business registration proof (incorporation certificate, GST, etc.)
